messages:
customer_jane: Hi team — starting ~06:15 UTC today our production app in eu-west-1 began returning ~20-30% 429s. Example request id r-9f2a3b attached. No config changes on our side. Can you advise quick mitigations?
support_maya: sorry you're hitting this, we're looking now. can you paste org id + sample request headers?
customer_jane: org: acmeops-prod. headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, X-Client-Version: sdk-js/2.1.3, X-Request-Id: r-9f2a3b. spikes are minute-aligned — looks like ~06:15, 07:15 etc.
eng_oncall_tim: thanks, I'm pulling the RPM/TPM counters for acmeops-prod. initial heatmap shows short bursts that line up with your timestamps. can you confirm SDK version? you mentioned 2.1.3 — is that widespread across pods?
customer_jane: yes all nodes on 2.1.3, rolled out last week.
devx_sam: quick hypothesis — we've seen an SDK refresh stampede pattern in 2.1.x where concurrent requests trigger parallel token refreshes after a 401, causing client-originated retry storms.
eng_oncall_tim: reading traces now — I see many requests from same client IP renewing tokens and then retrying in parallel; total effective concurrency spikes and trips per-org RPM cap -> 429.
qa_lee: repro suggestion (non-prod): run a concurrency test that simulates token expiry and post-401 refreshs. example using hey:
```
hey -n 500 -c 80 -H "Authorization: Bearer <expired>" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
this will show whether the client side is refreshing in parallel.
support_maya: short-term mitigation options: 1) we can temporarily raise your per-org RPM by 2x for 30m while you patch. 2) add an API gateway rule to rate-limit per-client to smooth spikes. 3) ensure client backs off on 429/401 with jittered exponential backoff. which would you prefer?
customer_jane: really need low-touch — can you do the quota bump while we patch? we'll roll a fix today.
eng_platform_zoe: I can apply a temporary RPM increase for acmeops-prod. requesting a 2x bump for 45 minutes, monitoring dashboards. putting a note in change log.
eng_oncall_tim: applied temporary bump (internal change id ch-74123). watch the rate graphs for 5m. also added a short ACL to limit parallel refresh endpoints to 10 rps per IP to prevent stampedes.
customer_jane: seeing 429s drop to near 0 in the last 3 minutes, thanks! :relieved: any concrete SDK patch guidance?
devx_sam: yes — fix is to serialize token refreshes (singleflight) and ensure retries use exponential backoff + full jitter. JS pseudocode: 
```
let refreshing = null;
async function getAuthHeader() {
  if (!token || token.expired) {
    if (!refreshing) refreshing = refreshToken();
    await refreshing;
    refreshing = null;
  }
  return `Bearer ${token.value}`;
}
```
For other languages use a mutex/lock or singleflight pattern.
qa_lee: also recommend adding client-side max concurrency for the endpoint (eg limit to 25 concurrent streams) and respecting Retry-After header on 429.
support_maya: for our internal follow-up, please send us: 1) minimal repro (hey/curl script), 2) sample SDK usage where refresh happens, 3) list of service instances on 2.1.3. we can keep the bump for a bit while you deploy.
customer_jane: we'll provide a repro and deploy a locked refresh later today. thanks for the rapid assist.
eng_platform_zoe: noted — I'll auto-revoke the temporary bump after 45m and keep monitoring. if you want an extended increase, we'll need an RFC/approval.
deploy_bot: deploy success: acmeops-prod patch v2.1.4 candidate queued to canary (deploy id d-741234).
eng_oncall_tim: follow-up items: - eng-platform to confirm bump removal timestamp - devx to publish SDK guidance and patch notes - support to confirm customer upgraded and 429s not returning. assigning ownership. :white_check_mark:
support_maya: closing loop with customer in 30m, ping us if anything reappears.
customer_jane: confirmed — post-patch + backoff + our fix, no more 429s in last 20m. thanks everyone! :thumbsup:
